field_changes.before: NIST's PQC Standardization Project (launched 2016) selected ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) as the first post-quantum standards, published August 2024. FN-DSA (FIPS 206) published March 2025. NIST IR 8547 defines the transition timeline: deprecate 112-bit classical asymmetric by 2030, disallow by 2035. NIST also runs CMVP (module validation) and CAVP (algorithm validation) programs that enforce these standards globally.

scope_summary: Normalised 29 vendor website values to absolute https:// URLs (vendors_07272026_r30.csv -> vendors_07292026.csv; VND-500..VND-528, the complete set of vendors ever minted by maintenance/register_vendor.py). Not cosmetic: generate-rag-corpus.ts uses the vendors `website` column verbatim as each vendor chunk's deepLink, and src/services/search/deepLinkGrammar.ts rejects a scheme-less string ('no route pattern matched'), which aborts the whole corpus build. Both `npm run refresh-index` and `npm run check-index-freshness` therefore exited 1 on main — the RAG search index could not be rebuilt at all, and the rag-index source's own freshness detector was dead. The failure was invisible because scripts/ci/check-index-freshness.ts runs the generator with stdio:'ignore', so the only symptom was a stack trace naming a child process with output:[null,null,null]. Root cause fixed the same day in register_vendor.py (it wrote domain.strip() into this column while already normalising the SAME --domain argument through its own _as_url helper for the trusted_sources row it writes — one input, two disagreeing CSVs); a vendors validator gate and two regression tests were added so a recurrence is reported against this source instead of surfacing three scripts downstream. Corpus build verified green afterwards: 13203 chunks, all 13151 deepLinks valid. Archived vendors_07182026.csv per the keep-2 rule. The other 498 rows in the file were already absolute and are byte-unchanged.

Maintenance-flow remediation, phase 0. Four defects, all the same class — a check reporting something it was not measuring. (1) generate-rag-corpus.ts reads passages from scripts/source-passages-*.json, which is gitignored and main-checkout-only; loadSourcePassages() returned an empty Map in silence when absent, so EVERY corpus regenerated from a git worktree dropped provenance from every chunk. Measured: 0 of 13203 chunks carried a passage. With the artifact present 576 do, and source_doc-without-passages falls 762 to 186. The corpus-trust-invariants C4 ratchet had been bumped four times (693, 695, 717, 725, 752), each annotated 'enrich to drive down' — enrichment could never have moved it. loadSourcePassages now warns loudly; MAX_DOC_WITHOUT_PASSAGES tightened to 186. (2) trustScoreData.ts built algorithm scores only from the transitions CSV, so 22 of 118 catalogued algorithms had no trust score at all — 17 of them hybrid/composite wire-format identifiers that nothing transitions TO. It now also scores from the reference catalogue it was already importing purely as a join. TIER_RESOLUTION_GAPS.algorithms 2 to 0. (3) Five timeline rows were silently dropped by timelineData.ts (blank Country at :225, or unparseable StartYear/EndYear at :227-229) and therefore never trust-scored. Two of them carry a 2026-07-24 note claiming this was already fixed — that backfill filled the org fields and left the years blank, and nobody noticed for five days because refresh-index had been failing, so the corpus these invariants test never changed. 4 of 5 completed from their own cached evidence documents plus their org's existing-row conventions (BSI meta datePublished 2025-10-31; NCSC 22 July 2026; NUKIB cached page 2026-07-08). The FAA row is deliberately left open and annotated: its only evidence is a fedscoop.com mirror that was REJECTED the same day for the trusted-sources registry, and inventing a country and a year to make a test go green is exactly what the proof gate exists to prevent. TIER_RESOLUTION_GAPS.timeline 3 to 1. (4) 28 non-canonical Source_Type values canonicalised in pqc_authoritative_sources_reference_07292026.csv, mapped per row against the registry's own existing conventions rather than by string substitution. Also: 3 deprecated learner-facing standardIds re-pointed through their machine-readable superseded_by chains (the 4th has no successor and went to the proposal flow); reference-cache drift report regenerated after 5 days stale (411 ok of 1032, down from 442 of 967); RAG index rebuilt and re-signed. Full hub suite green — 4742 tests, 0 failures; all audit/validate gates pass; 8 attestations verified.

RAG provenance restored. extract-source-passages.py had produced nothing usable since the 2026-07-12 local-evidence-cache relocation, so every corpus built in that window carried ZERO source_passages on all ~13k chunks. Three independent path bugs, any one fatal: CSVs were sought in pqctoday-priv/src/data (which does not exist — they live in the hub); local_file resolved against the repo root instead of pqctoday-priv/local-evidence-cache/; and the _rN revision suffix sorted as a STRING, so with library_07282026_r9.csv and _r10.csv both present it picked r9, the older file (the MMDDYYYY date was compared whole too, which would mis-sort across a year boundary). Plus a wrong CSV prefix for threats, and — the dangerous one — it wrote its empty result to a NEW dated file that loadSourcePassages() then prefers, so a broken run actively destroyed provenance. It now refuses to write an artifact containing zero passages. Result: 886 of 976 library records resolve (was 0), 879 got passages, corpus chunks carrying passages 576 -> 751, and the C4 ratchet MAX_DOC_WITHOUT_PASSAGES 187 -> 12.

Four approved auto-fixes plus two investigations. (1) 7 protocol-matrix stage advances applied, each confirmed against a FRESH datatracker poll — the check run had been reading a 2026-07-27 report that disagreed with the current matrix in both directions. ike-ipsec:hybridKem was deliberately EXCLUDED from the 8 the applier offered: its own note records a human correcting it to 'draft', and the datatracker resolves RFC 9370, the multi-KE FRAMEWORK, not a hybrid-KEM RFC. (2) enrich-protocol-matrix.py resolved a document's type against the wrong API namespace (/api/v1/doc/... where the datatracker returns /api/v1/name/...), so RFC refs NEVER resolved to rfc-published and could never suppress a sibling draft's apparent downgrade. That produced two permanent false regressions, re-triaged every run: ssh:hybridKem (RFC 9941 published) and cose:pureSig (RFC 9964 published), both correctly encoded while tracking a follow-on draft still in progress. Fixed; remaining backward deltas 2 -> 0. (3) 4 library local_file paths corrected .pdf -> .html — eCFR pages that never served a PDF, whose .html copies were already on disk beside the path the CSV named (109-686KB, verified titles). The other 3 rows the same validator flags were deliberately NOT renamed: they point at URLs genuinely ending .pdf, so the HTML is probably a consent/paywall page and renaming would file a block page as evidence while looking fixed. (4) lint-staged no longer tries to git-add into the gitignored src/data/archive, which printed a scary FAILED on every archival commit.

Digital ID module audit remediation, data half. THREE new dated CSVs. library_07312026.csv: new access_type + free_summary_url columns; 21 rows marked access_type=paid (ISO/IEC/IEEE SA/ANSI/SAE) so a purchase page is never presented as a download, with free summaries on 17 of them; IEEE-802-1AE un-marked (the 802 series is free via the IEEE GET Program, so the hostname rule was too coarse); 5 dead download_urls repaired; 4 rows restored that had been switched off for reasons the paid-source policy supersedes (ISO-18013-5-mDL was deprecated 07-26 by a Cloudflare bot-block misread as a dead link, and the ANSI pair reverses a deliberate 07-30 call, knowingly and on request). THREE fabricated PQC standards deprecated after verification against the publishers' own pages: IEEE-P1931-1-ROSA (P1931.1 is the ROOF IoT framework, not PQC; no standard named ROSA exists), ISO/IEC NP 29192-8 (is 29192-8:2022 Authenticated encryption, published, not PQC), and IEEE 1609.2 Amendment (no such project). A fourth was corrected rather than hidden: ISO/IEC 18033-2 Amd 1 claimed 'Post-Quantum KEMs' and its URL pointed at ISO 8144-1:2026, mineral wool thermal insulation — Amd 1 is FACE (classical); the PQC content is Amd 2. Also fixed two false claims that were rendering to users: the ARF row asserted a PQC roadmap the ARF does not contain, and the ISO 18013-5 row credited eu.europa.ec.eudi.pid.1 to ISO. compliance_07312026.csv: new learn_modules column, populated on 6 rows where the mapping is defensible, so a framework can route a reader into the module teaching it (traversal was one-way). timeline_07312026.csv: authored the missing EU row 'EUDI Wallet Available in All Member States' (2026) — the Digital ID module's headline deadline had no timeline row at all, so it could not be derived from the single source of truth even in principle. Prior generations archived, 2-generation cap held on all three. New validators: C4R (module standards -> library, the reverse of C4), C4P (paid rows marked and not shown as downloads), C4T (deadlines -> timeline event_id with year agreement). Each was verified to FAIL on an injected or pre-existing fault rather than pass vacuously.
